units.la: DISSERTATIO THEOLOGICA, DE ΚΑΤΗΧΗΣΙ[?] HOMINIS CHRISTIANI.
units.tr: THEOLOGICAL DISSERTATION ON THE CHRISTIAN'S BOASTING [καύχησις]

units.la: Ita naturâ comparatum est, ut quae bona mortales possident, iis non tantùm delectentur sibiquè propter ea gratulentur, sed etiam eorum mentes suavitate illarum rerum demulsae ac gaudio tumultuquè plenae citiùs non conquiescant, donec etiam suae fælicitatis aliis ideam dederint, plausumquè aliorum sibi congratulantium invenerint; Hinc potens hujus mundi de sua gloriatur potentia, cùm sit impotentissimum affectuum suorum mancipium; gloriatur eruditus de sua scientia, qui tamen ignobilis noctuae instar in rebus spiritualibus caecutit; sic Matheseos studiis innutritus admirandâ numerorum proportionis ac corporum spatiorumve dimensionis scientiâ turgens exultat, qui tamen cum omnibus sanctis nunquam vel cogitatione attigit quod sit τὸ πλάτος καὶ μῆκος καὶ βάθος καὶ ὕψος amoris Dei, Eph.3:18. At quam vanum, futile & stultum hoc gloriandi genus in rebus tam fluxis & perituris, quae dum nascuntur, iterum evanescunt; Et quàm pravam matrem hæc pessima filia habet! ambitionem scilicet, quæ Bernhardo dicitur subtile malum, secretum virus, mater hypocriseos, livoris parens, vitiorum origo, criminum fomes, virtutum ærugo, tinea sanctitatis. Longè aliter fideles gloriantur non quidem de bonis caducis hujus sæculi, sed de permanentibus illis in æternum, non de justitia sibi propria, sed de illa Christi perfectissima, non jactantes sed humiles; Et hæc est illa gloriatio, quæ sola solida soliquè[?] homini Christiano conveniens est, cujus etiam naturam ac indolem impræsentiarum bono cum Deo rudi licet penicillo adumbrare studebimus.
units.tr: It is so ordered by nature that mortals take delight in the good things they possess and rejoice in them, and that their minds, soothed by the sweetness of those things and filled with joy and commotion, cannot rest until they have also given others some idea of their happiness and received the applause of others who congratulate them. Hence the powerful man of this world boasts of his power, though he is the most powerless slave of his own passions. The learned man boasts of his learning, though like an ignoble owl he is blind in spiritual matters. So one who has been nurtured in the study of mathematics swells and exults in his wonderful science of number, proportion and the measurement of bodies and spaces, yet he has never, even in thought, touched what the breadth and length and depth and height of the love of God are (Eph. 3:18) [τὸ πλάτος καὶ μῆκος καὶ βάθος καὶ ὕψος], along with all the saints. But how vain, frivolous and foolish is this kind of boasting in things so fleeting and perishable, which vanish again as soon as they are born! And how wicked a mother this worst daughter has! I mean ambition, which Bernard calls a subtle evil, a hidden poison, the mother of hypocrisy, the parent of envy, the origin of vices, the kindling of crimes, the rust of virtues, the moth of holiness. Believers boast quite differently: not of the fleeting goods of this age, but of those that endure forever; not of a righteousness of their own, but of Christ's most perfect righteousness; boasting not arrogantly but humbly. This is the boasting that alone is solid and fitting for a Christian man, and at present we shall try to sketch its nature and character, though with a rough brush, with God's blessing.
II.

units.la: Hæc vero καύχησις nihil aliud est quàm abnegatâ propriâ justitiâ magna cum fiducia corde confiteri, nec minori cum lætitia ore profiteri se habere in Christo justitiam sive jus ad vitam æternam. De hac gloriatione jam vaticinatus erat Esaias cap.45:25. Propheta Christum introducebat in hæc verba fantem: Respicite intentò sc. veræ fidei oculo ad me, qui solus sum Jehovah, in quo sunt צדקות perfectissima justitia & robur, & salvamini omnes fines terræ; postea autem addit omnes accessuros etiam gloriaturos in Domino, dicens: in Domino יתהללו gloriabuntur omne semen Israelis, h. e. totus Israël Dei Gal. 6:6. omnes filii promissionis Rom. 9:8. se felices prædicabunt & coram omnibus lætabundo animo confitebuntur se habere in Domino justitiam sive jus ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: This boasting [καύχησις] is nothing other than, with one's own righteousness renounced, to confess with the heart, in great confidence, and with no less joy to profess with the mouth, that one has in Christ righteousness, or a right to eternal life. Isaiah had already prophesied of this boasting in chapter 45:25. The prophet introduces Christ speaking these words: "Look to me," that is, with the eye of true faith, "who alone am Jehovah, in whom are [צדקות] perfect righteousness and strength; and be saved, all you ends of the earth." Afterwards he adds that all who approach will also glory in the Lord, saying: "In Jehovah [יתהללו] all the seed of Israel shall glory" (Gal. 6:16), that is, all Israel of God, all the children of promise (Rom. 9:8). They will declare themselves happy and will confess with a joyful mind before everyone that they have in the Lord righteousness, or a right to eternal life.
III.

units.la: Gloriari autem in genere est de se rem bonam dicere vel aliquid magni de se prædicare; Chrysostomus ait μεγάλα γὰρ ἑαυτῷ φθέγξαιτο[?]; gloriaturum igitur coram Deo etiam magni quid & praeclari de se praedicare oportebit; quale vero id esse posset, quo cum coram Deo comparere ac subsistere possit, aliud quàm perfectissima omnibusque numeris absoluta obedientia sanctissimae Dei legi praestita, cujus summa est Deum amare ex toto corde & proximum sicut seipsum? Matth. 22:36,37. huic enim soli Deus addixit justitiam & vitam, Lev. 18:5. Rom. 7:10. illiusque solius impletio causa esse potest juris exspectandi haereditatem & petendi vitam aeternam.
units.tr: To glory in general is to say something good about oneself or to proclaim something great about oneself. Chrysostom says: "for he might say great things of himself" [μεγάλα γὰρ ἑαυτῷ φθέγξαιτο]. So one who is to glory before God will have to proclaim something great and excellent about himself. But what could this be, by which he could come into God's presence and stand before him, other than the most perfect obedience, absolute in every respect, rendered to God's most holy law, whose sum is to love God with the whole heart and one's neighbour as oneself (Matt. 22:36, 37)? For God has assigned righteousness and life to this alone (Lev. 18:5; Rom. 7:10), and the fulfilment of this alone can be the ground of a right to expect the inheritance and to ask for eternal life.
IV.

units.la: Hoc cùm sit fundamentum gloriationis, jure merito quaeri potest, an homo id habeat à seipso, an verò ab alio? An propterea propriis suis meritis confisus gloriari,an verò gloriationem, si quam habere vellet, in alio quaerere teneatur? Illud quidem potuisset Adamus, si examussim legem divinam observasset dicendo: quae debui facere, feci Luc. 17:10. gloriam Dei quaesivi, Joh. 5:44. nomen Dei amavi, Psal. 5:12. ideò vi promissionis divinae reposita mihi est vita ex merito & ὀφειλήματι, Rom. 4:4. At proh dolor! Miser ille homo mutabilis quidem creatus, astutiâ & dolo tentatoris hanc legem transgressus, pulchritudine imaginis Dei, & per consequens quoque legem servandi facultate destitutus hoc jure excidit seque omnigenae mortis reum fecit, juxta Gen. 3. Rom. 5:12.
units.tr: Since this is the foundation of boasting, it may rightly be asked whether man has it from himself or from another. Is he bound to trust in his own merits and glory in them, or is he bound to seek whatever boasting he would have in another? Adam could indeed have done so, had he observed the divine law exactly, saying: "I have done what I ought to have done" (Luke 17:10); "I have sought the glory of God" (John 5:44); "I have loved the name of God" (Ps. 5:12); therefore by the force of the divine promise life is laid up for me as a matter of merit and debt (Rom. 4:4). But alas! That wretched man, created indeed changeable, through the cunning and deceit of the tempter transgressed this law, and, deprived of the beauty of the image of God and consequently also of the ability to keep the law, he fell from this right and made himself liable to every kind of death (according to Gen. 3; Rom. 5:12).
V.

units.la: Nec meliorem sortem nacti sunt omnes ejus posteri vi illius verbi crescite & multiplicamini nascituri: πάντες γὰρ ἡμαρτον [?] καὶ ὑστερεῖνται [?] τῆς δόξης τῷ Θεῷ, Rom. 3:23. Hinc non tantum vocantur τέκνα φύσει ὀργῆς, Eph. 2:3. quia geniti sunt sub ira, haeredes irae sicque irâ Dei certissimè persequendi, quemadmodum filii mortis dicitur qui mortis reus vel morti destinatus ac infallibiliter morte absorbendus est; ira enim Dei manet super omnes, qui Evangelio non obediunt, Joh. 3:26. Verum etiam mortui τοῖς παραπτώμασι [?] καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν, Eph. 2:1. utpote qui vita Dei privati à semetipsis tanquam ex semetipsis nihil boni cogitare possunt, 2. Cor. 3:5. neque se legi Dei subjicere, Rom. 8:7. homo enim ψυχικὸς i. e. nil nisi animam habens spiritumque Dei illuminante, regenerante, sanctificante destitutus [?] τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ Θεοῦ, 1. Cor. 2:14. Huc pertinet infallibile illud Dei ipsius testimonium, quod extat Gen. 6:5. & Jehovah vidit i. e. probè perspexit, consideravit, non aliquod tantum, sed omne figmentum cordis humani, non aliquando, sed omni die, non aliquatenus, sed tantummodo malum esse: Hinc Apostolus dicet τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατος, i. e. quicquid caro sentit, sapit, studet, mors est, i. e. in se mortiferum, mortem adducit. Rom. 8:7.
units.tr: Nor did all his posterity, born by the force of that word "increase and multiply," obtain a better lot: "for all have sinned and come short of the glory of God" (Rom. 3:23) [πάντες γὰρ ἡμαρτον καὶ ὑστερεῖνται τῆς δόξης τῷ Θεῷ]. Hence they are called "children of wrath by nature" (Eph. 2:3) [τέκνα φύσει ὀργῆς], because they were born under wrath, heirs of wrath, and so most certainly to be pursued by the wrath of God; just as one is called a "son of death" who is liable to death or destined for death and is infallibly to be swallowed up by death. For the wrath of God remains upon all who do not obey the Gospel (John 3:36). Indeed they are also "dead in trespasses and sins" (Eph. 2:1) [τοῖς παραπτώμασι καὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν], since, deprived of the life of God, they cannot of themselves, as from themselves, think anything good (2 Cor. 3:5), nor do they subject themselves to the law of God (Rom. 8:7). For the natural man [ψυχικὸς], that is, one who has only a soul and is destitute of the Spirit of God, who illuminates, regenerates and sanctifies, does not receive the things of the Spirit of God (1 Cor. 2:14) [τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ Θεοῦ]. To this belongs that infallible testimony of God himself, found in Gen. 6:5: "And Jehovah saw," that is, thoroughly perceived and considered, not some only but "every imagination of the thoughts of the heart" of man, not at some time but "every day," not in some measure but that it was "only evil." Hence the Apostle says that "the mind of the flesh is death" (Rom. 8:7) [τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατος], that is, whatever the flesh perceives, savours or aims at is death, that is, deadly in itself, bringing death.
VI.

units.la: Haec autem corruptio tanta est in omnibus, quotquot nascuntur filii Adami, ut vocentur δοῦλοι τῆς ἁμαρτίας, Rom. 6:16, 17, 19. & Joh. 5:34, 36. homo enim jugô obedientiae Deo debitae excussô alium Dominum, potius dicam tyrannum, quem ipsemet elegit, natus est, peccatum scilicet uti id nobis passim ab Apostolo Paulo sub hac σχέσει proponitur, imprimis autem Rom. 5. & 6. ubi ei introitus in mundum, c. 5:22, regnum, c. 6:12. arma,v.13. servi, v.16. & stipendium, v.23 adscribuntur; quod ita fortiter omnibus dominatur, ut à seipsis nihil agant, quin imò nihil agere velint quàm peccare,haud secus ac servus omnia, quæ agit, ex præscripto Domini facit,ita eodem planè modo homo quicquid agit, ex præscripto peccati in membris suis regnantis facit; id quod fit justâ Dei sententiâ, à quo enim quis superatus est, quemadmodum homo à peccato, ei in servitatem est addictus, 2.Pet.2:19. in qua manere debet, usquedum alius peccato fortior eum è potestate ejus eripiat. Hinc etiam peccatum in judicio Dei adversus peccatorem contendens, uti ita nobis depingitur, Rom.8:3. ut æternùm ei dominetur, non potuit, quamdiu legi nondum satisfactum erat, condemnari i. e. petitio ac accusatio ejus injusta iniquave pronuntiari, allegat enim pro se justam Dei legem, quæ peccatorem maledictum & corruptelæ servum pronuntiat: propterea lex, quæ prima fronte quàm maximè peccato contraria videtur, dicitur δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας, 1.Cor.15:56. quia peccatum armat contra peccatorem, ita ut Deus judicans juxta tenorem legis peccato concedat dominium in peccatorem; quin imò sapienter admodum & ἐμφατικὸς ipsa sanctissima Dei lex νόμῳ τῆς ἁμαρτίας à Paulo vocatur Rom 8:2. Non quasi peccatum aliquod permitteret, multò minùs præciperet, sed quia justâ suâ sententiâ peccatorem peccato, tyrannidem in eum exercenti mancipat atque adjudicat haud aliter ac lex mariti appellatur ea, quæ mulierem marito vindicat, Rom.7:2.3.
units.tr: This corruption is so great in all who are born as sons of Adam that they are called "servants of sin" (Rom. 6:16, 17, 19; John 5:34, 36) [δοῦλοι τῆς ἁμαρτίας]. For a man, having shaken off the yoke of the obedience owed to God, is born under another lord, or rather tyrant, whom he has chosen for himself, namely sin, as the Apostle Paul presents it to us everywhere under this relation, especially in Rom. 5 and 6, where entrance into the world is ascribed to it (5:12), reign (6:12), weapons (6:13), servants (6:16) and wages (6:23). It so strongly dominates all men that of themselves they do nothing, and indeed they wish to do nothing but sin. Just as a servant does everything he does by his master's order, so in exactly the same way a man does whatever he does by the order of sin reigning in his members. This comes about by the just sentence of God: "for of whom a man is overcome," as a man is overcome by sin, "of the same he is brought into bondage" (2 Pet. 2:19), and in that bondage he must remain until someone stronger than sin rescues him from its power. Hence also sin, contending in God's judgment against the sinner, as is depicted for us in Rom. 8:3, could not be "condemned" as long as the law had not yet been satisfied, that is, its petition and accusation against him could not be pronounced unjust or wicked. For it pleads for itself the just law of God, which pronounces the sinner accursed and a slave of corruption. Therefore the law, which at first sight seems most opposed to sin, is called "the power of sin" (1 Cor. 15:56) [δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας], because sin arms itself against the sinner, so that God, judging according to the tenor of the law, grants sin dominion over the sinner. Indeed, very wisely and emphatically, the most holy law of God itself is called by Paul "the law of sin" (Rom. 8:2) [νόμῳ τῆς ἁμαρτίας]. Not as though it permitted any sin, much less commanded it, but because by its just sentence it hands over and adjudges the sinner to sin, which exercises tyranny over him. It is no differently than the law of the husband is the name given to that which binds a woman to her husband (Rom. 7:2, 3).
VII.

units.la: Quod si ita fit, πῶς ἂν ἡ καύχησις; quæ hominem propriis suis nixum operibus ac meritis manere posset, respondet Apostolus: ἐξεκλείσθη Rom.3,27. qui in precedentibus in eo erat, ut ostenderet omnes tam Judæos quàm gentes sub peccato esse conclusos, id autem ut probet multa scripturæ loca citat in quibus graphicè omnimoda hominis corruptio depingitur; cum autem Judæi superbi & jactabundi facilimè excipere potuisfent, hæc ipsos non tangere, huic cogitationi occurrit, v.19. dicens: illa, quæ lex dicit, dici iis, qui sunt sub lege, & per consequens etiam Judæis; unde infert v.20. nullam carnem justificari ex operibus legis tam moralis, quippe quàm transgressa est, multisque modis transgreditur quotidie, à qua etiam condemnatur reatuique subjicitur, quàm ceremonialis, quæ non semper fuit, nec etiam quando fuit, quenquam justificare potuit, Act.13:39. ut nec consummare, Heb.7:19. nec peccata auferre, Heb.10:1,4,11. quin per legem est agnitio peccati, Rom.3:20. sed hominem justificari gratis ipsius gratia per redemtionem quæ est in Christo Jesu. v.24. ποῦ οὖν ἡ καύχησις; quaerit tandem Apostolus, illa sc. quæ est πρὸς τὸν Θεόν, Rom.4,2. ἐξεκλείσθη exclusa est.
units.tr: But if that is so, how can there be boasting, which would allow a man resting on his own works and merits to stand? The Apostle answers: boasting was shut out [ἐξεκλείσθη] (Rom. 3:27). In the preceding verses his aim was to show that all, both Jews and Gentiles, are shut up under sin. To prove this he cites many passages of Scripture that vividly depict the complete corruption of man. But since the proud and boastful Jews could easily have objected that these things did not touch them, he meets this thought in verse 19, saying: what the law says, it says to those who are under the law, and so, by implication, to the Jews as well. Hence he infers in verse 20 that no flesh is justified by the works of the law. This holds of the moral law, which man has transgressed and daily transgresses in many ways, and by which he is therefore condemned and made liable to guilt. It also holds of the ceremonial law, which was not always in force, and which, even when it was, could not justify anyone (Acts 13:39), nor bring to completion (Heb. 7:19), nor take away sins (Heb. 10:1, 4, 11). Indeed, through the law comes the knowledge of sin (Rom. 3:20). Instead, man is justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus (v. 24). Finally, the Apostle asks: where then is boasting? namely that boasting which is before God (Rom. 4:2). It was shut out [ἐξεκλείσθη].
VIII.

units.la: Proinde si quis fretus suis operibus & meritis vellet comparere & indutus ornamento propriæ justitiæ gloriari coram Domino, de ejusmodi hominis salute jam conclamatum foret, utpote qui coram eo stare non possit, si pravitates serves Domine, quis stabit? i.e. nemo. Psal.130:3. nam nos nostri nihil habemus nisi peccatum, כל נשמ[?] quicquid enim accipis nil nisi pravitas est, Hos. 14:2. Si qui cum alieno igne accedebat ad tabernaculum terrestre, iram Dei non effugiebat: quid impetrabit ille, qui cum peccatis suis tanquam acceptus Deo & cum sua propria justitia ad Deum accedere ausus fuerit? in contradictionem Core incidet inque ea peribit, Jud. v.ii. Unde David profunda cum humilitate nullitatem ac impotentiam suam confitens deprecatur: ne venias Domine in judicium cum servo tuo, nam apud te nullus vivens justificatur, Psal.143:2. Deus enim cum homine in judicium veniens non aliter judicare potest quam secundum sanctissimam suam legem ab homine postulantem, ut omnia praecepta debito modo atque constanter servet; homo autem per peccatum imagine Dei & sic etiam facultate Deum ex toto corde amandi privatus debitum amorem Dei in judicium afferre nequit, ideo etiam nec justificari & ad vitam aeternam admitti. Sic etiam Paulus, cui tamen si ulli carne gloriari licuisset, nolebat habere justitiam, quae erat ex lege. Phil.3:6,9.
units.tr: Therefore, if anyone, trusting in his own works and merits, wished to appear before God and glory in the ornament of his own righteousness, his salvation would at once be pronounced hopeless, since he could not stand before him. If you, Lord, should mark iniquities, who shall stand? That is, no one (Ps. 130:3). For we have nothing of our own but sin. Whatever you receive is nothing but wickedness (Hos. 14:2). Whoever approached the earthly tabernacle with strange fire did not escape the wrath of God. What will he obtain who dares to come before God with his sins as if he were acceptable, and with his own righteousness? He will fall into the rebellion of Korah and perish in it (Jude v. 11). So David, with deep humility, confessing his nothingness and powerlessness, pleads: do not enter into judgment with your servant, for in your sight no living man is justified (Ps. 143:2). For God, when he comes into judgment with a man, can judge only according to his most holy law, which requires a man to keep all the precepts in the due manner and constantly. But man, through sin, has lost the image of God, and with it the ability to love God with his whole heart. Therefore he cannot bring the love of God owed to judgment, and so cannot be justified or admitted to eternal life. So too Paul, who, if anyone had reason to glory in the flesh, had it, yet did not want to have the righteousness which is of the law (Phil. 3:6, 9).
IX.

units.la: Si quis vero vim suam facturus Deum suum, Hab.1:11. haec de irregenito tantum dici crediderit, non vero de regenito, qui multa bona opera praestare possit, sicque in iis tanquam causa justitiae suae gloriari coram Domino. Is sciat oportet, quod quicquid homo praestat, id non agat proprio Marte, sed Dei auxilio, aut quid habes O homo? quod non acceperis, εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔλαβες τί καυχᾶσαι ὡς μὴ λαβών, 1.Cor.4:7. quin bona regenitorum opera sunt fructus justitiae Christi, non ad gloriam nostram, verum εἰς δόξαν καὶ ἔπαινον Θεοῦ, Phil.1:11. Christus enim sua justitia nobis Spiritum Sanctum, qui operatur in nobis καὶ τὸ θέλειν καὶ τὸ ἐνεργεῖν, Phil.2:13. impetravit; ipsaque justitia Christi insigne motivum est ad fructus eâ dignos proferendos; nunc autem quàm absonum est dicere fructum esse ipsam arborem vel causam arboris, tàm absurdum etiam est afferere, bona opera, quæ sunt fructus justitiæ, esse ipsam justitiam vel causam justitiæ: nam non ideò justi sumus, quia bonis operibus operam damus, sed ideò bona præstamus opera iisquè gratiâs agimus Deo, quia justi sumus: Denique omnia nostra bona opera propter τὴν εὐπερίστασιν ἁμαρτίαν[?], Heb.12:1. quod ad mortem usquè in nobis stabulatur, quàm maximè sunt imperfecta, variisque nævis ac viciis infecta, totusquè cultus noster defectuosus, hinc justitiæ nostræ comparantur cum panno menstruato, Esa.64:6. Lex autem iis, qui omnia plane, plenè & ad finem usquè absquè ullo defectu & cespitatione, quæ legis sunt, faciunt, vitam addicit: ideò ex bonis nostris operibus nullam jactandi, sed potiùs nos humiliandi causam habemus.
units.tr: But if someone, making his own might his god (Hab. 1:11), believes that this is said only of the unregenerate and not of the regenerate, who can perform many good works and so glory in them as the cause of his righteousness before the Lord, let him know this: whatever a man does, he does not act by his own power but by the help of God. What do you have, O man, that you have not received? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it? [εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔλαβες τί καυχᾶσαι ὡς μὴ λαβών] (1 Cor. 4:7). Moreover, the good works of the regenerate are the fruits of Christ's righteousness, not for our glory but to the glory and praise of God [εἰς δόξαν καὶ ἔπαινον Θεοῦ] (Phil. 1:11). For Christ, by his righteousness, obtained for us the Holy Spirit, who works in us both to will and to work [καὶ τὸ θέλειν καὶ τὸ ἐνεργεῖν] (Phil. 2:13). The righteousness of Christ itself is a notable motive for bringing forth fruits worthy of it. Now, just as it is absurd to say that the fruit is the tree itself or the cause of the tree, so it is equally absurd to assert that good works, which are the fruits of righteousness, are themselves righteousness or its cause. For we are not righteous because we devote ourselves to good works. Rather, we perform good works and give thanks to God because we are righteous. Finally, all our good works, because of the sin which so easily entangles us [τὴν εὐπερίστασιν ἁμαρτίαν] (Heb. 12:1), which dwells within us until death, are most imperfect and stained with various blemishes and vices. Our whole worship is defective. Hence our righteousness is compared to a menstrual cloth (Isa. 64:6). But the law promises life only to those who do everything completely, fully, and to the end, without any defect or stumbling in what the law requires. Therefore we have no cause for boasting in our good works, but rather for humbling ourselves.
X.

units.la: Equidem haud diffiteor, si postulatum legis inexorabilemquè Dei justitiam tantùm respicias, omnem gloriationem ex propriis operibus præcisam esse; aliquam verò superesse, si ejusdem attendas misericordiam, quâ Deus mancam mutilamquè obedientiam pro consummata acceptare, nævosquè ei adhærescentes conniventibus oculis aspicere promittit; perinde ac benignus pater affectu paterno conatus bonamquè filiorum suorum voluntatem pro opere ipso reputat, nec minùs munificè mercedem iis rependit, ac si obedientiam omnibus numeris absolutam præstitissent. Verùm hac ratione non tàm tuâ gloriareris justitiâ quàm Dei misericordia ricordiâ: Deinde est quidem Deus misericors, sed sine ullo tamen justitiae suae dispendio, quae postulat ut jus legis impleatur in omnibus vitae aeternae haeredibus, Rom.8:3. propterea etiam Deus nomen suum Mosi & Israëli, à gratia, misericordia & longanimitate explicaturus illico addit נקה לא ינקה nocentem minime impunitum dimittet, Exod 34:6,7. Misericordia Dei itaque non in eo versatur, quod imperfectam obedientiam pro perfecta acceperet, eique vitam addicat; Sic enim per fidem misericordiae legem redderemus inanem, contra Rom.3:31. nec ita justitia Dei demonstraretur, sed potius abnegaretur v.26. sed in eo quod Deus nobis miseris peccatoribus justitiâ Dei carentibus ex pura puta gratia mediatorem admisit, excitavit & aeternam ejus justitiam impletione legis adductam impertit, quô Deus ostendit τὸν ὑπερβάλλοντα πλοῦτον τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἐν χρηστότητι ἐφ' ἡμᾶς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, Eph.2:7. thronusq; gratiae in sanguine suŏ Pontificis nomĕdei sanctificantis, erectus manet thronus sanctitatis, Pf.47:9. ad quem tantum Κρατοῦντες τὴν ὁμολογίαν accedere debent ad consequendam misericordiam & inveniendam gratiam ad opportunum auxilium, Heb. 4:14,16.
units.tr: Indeed I do not deny that if you look only at the demand of the law and the inexorable justice of God, all boasting in one's own works is cut off. But some boasting remains if you consider God's mercy. By this mercy God promises to accept a lame and maimed obedience as complete, and to look with indulgent eyes upon the blemishes that cling to it. So a kind father, moved by fatherly affection, counts the good will of his sons as the deed itself, and rewards them no less generously than if they had rendered obedience in every respect complete. Yet in this way you would not glory so much in your own righteousness as in the mercy of God. Furthermore, God is indeed merciful, but without any loss to his justice, which demands that the right of the law be fulfilled in all the heirs of eternal life (Rom. 8:3). Therefore God, when he was about to declare his name to Moses and Israel as one of grace, mercy, and long-suffering, immediately added: he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished (Exod. 34:6, 7). Thus the mercy of God does not consist in his accepting imperfect obedience as perfect and granting life on that basis. For in that case, through faith, we would make the law void (Rom. 3:31), and the justice of God would not be shown but rather denied (v. 26). Rather, God's mercy consists in this: that out of pure grace he gave us wretched sinners, who lacked the righteousness of God, a mediator, raised him up, and bestowed on us his eternal righteousness, brought about by the fulfilment of the law. In this God displays the surpassing riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus [ὑπερβάλλοντα πλοῦτον τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἐν χρηστότητι ἐφ' ἡμᾶς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ] (Eph. 2:7). The throne of grace, set up in the blood of his sanctifying high priest, remains the throne of holiness (Ps. 47:9). Only those who hold fast the confession [Κρατοῦντες τὴν ὁμολογίαν] should approach it, to obtain mercy and find grace for timely help (Heb. 4:14, 16).
XI.

units.la: Ne igitur glorietur sapiens in sapientia sua, & ne glorietur fortis in fortitudine sua, ne glorietur dives in divitiis suis, Jerem.9:24. imo ne glorietur ulla caro coram eo, sed qui gloriatur ἐν κυρίῳ καυχάσθω, 1.Cor.1:29,31. 2.Cor.10:17. Non amplius in se, in quo omnis propriae gloriationis ratio exclusa, sed in alio utique gloriandi materia quaerere tenetur, qui solide gloriari cupit; in eo scilicet in quo sunt צדקות consummatissimum jus sive omnia jura ad vitam æternam, Esa. 45:24. qui est servus ille justus, qui multos justificaturus erat, Esa 53. v. 11. & adducturus צֶדֶק עוֹלָמִים justitiam sæculorum, i. e. justitiam sufficientem omnibus sæculis, cujusque effecta in omnem æternitatem duratura essent; qui sanè nullus alius esse poterit, quàm Rex noster מָשִׁיחַ [?] unctus, Christus Dan. 9:24. vel consentientibus ipsis apertis Christi hostibus Judæis, qui Messiam מָשִׁיחַ צִדְקֵנוּ [?] justitiam nostram vocant; Is enim Christus scilicet ἐγενήθη ἡμῖν δικαιοσύνη extitit & revera compertus est nobis esse justitia, 1.Cor.11,30. quippe qui formâ servi acceptâ obedientiâ suâ perfectissimâ legi charitatis satisfecit, ac utrumque præceptum de amore Dei & proximi exactissimè ad ultimum usquè vitæ halitum servavit; Amor autem, quem debebat Deo, Christum obligabat, postquàm sub legem factus erat, ad quærendam Dei gloriam & ad eam quantùm pote illustrandam, quod quoque à Christo præstitum ex tota Evangelii historia quàm clarissimè constat; Is enim est, qui jam in pueritia diligenter curavit ἐν τοῖς [?] τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ Luc. 2:40, 49. regnumquè Dei prædicans, Matth. 4. sanctissimam ejus legem à falsis Pharisæorum glossis vindicans. Matth. 5. voluntatemquè mittentis eum summa cum voluptate executus, Joh. 4:34. factusquè obediens ad mortem usquè, mortem autem crucis, Phil. 2:8. nomen i. e. perfectiones ejus patefecit, ac nominatim ejus veritatem, bonitatem, sapientiam, justitiam, sanctitatem, & omnisufficientem tanquam in augusto theatro omnium contemplationi expositi, adeò ut ex hoc opere gloria Dei magis quàm ex ullo alio, imò vel ipsius creationis opere eluxerit; Quemadmodum autem Christus non gloriam suam, sed τὴν δόξαν τῷ πέμψαντί αὐτοῦ [?] quæ-sivit, sivit, Joh. 7:18. ita etiam non quaesivit, quae sua, sed quae proximi sunt, 1.Cor. 13:19. cujus frater vocari non erubuit. Heb. 2:11. Hunc enim tanto persecutus est affectu, ut vitam suam pro eo ponere non dubitaverit, quâ certè charitate nemo majorem habet, Christo ipso teste, quàm ut quis animam suam ponat ὑπὲρ τῶν φίλων αὐτοῦ [?] Joh. 15:13. sed Dominus Jesus omni humano affectu superior κατάρα [?] factus fuit. Gal. 3:13. i.e. hostia & sacrificium pro maledictione, ejusque vivum, quasi exemplar ac imago, in quantum homo sanctus & Dominus gloriae talis fieri potuit, extitit, omnem maledictionis vim in corpore & anima sentiens; quin imò mortuus est pro nobis, dum adhuc in nobis ipsis considerati ἀσεβεῖς ἁμαρτωλοὶ & ejus ἐχθροί eramus. Rom. 5. v. 6,9,10. O Ingens Amor! O Charitas immensa! ὑπὲρ βάλλουσαν τῆς γνώσεως, cujus πλάτος καὶ μῆκος, καὶ βάθος καὶ ὕψος [?] nemo assequi potest, Eph. 3:18,19. & sic lex Dei erat in medio viscerum ejus, i.e. omne legis δικαιώματα adimplevit Ps. 40:9. quod egregiè jam praefiguratum fuit per utramque legis tabulam arcae inclusam, Exod. 34. vers. 16,17. Hebr. 9. vers. 4.
units.tr: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, nor the strong man glory in his strength, nor the rich man glory in his riches (Jer. 9:24). Indeed, let no flesh glory before him; but whoever glories, let him glory in the Lord [ἐν κυρίῳ καυχάσθω] (1 Cor. 1:29, 31; 2 Cor. 10:17). He who desires to glory solidly must no longer seek the ground of glorying in himself, in whom all grounds of self-glorying are shut out, but in another, namely in him in whom are tsidqot [צדקות], the most perfect right, or all the rights to eternal life (Isa. 45:24). This is that righteous servant who was to justify many (Isa. 53:11), and who would bring in tsedeq olamim [צֶדֶק עוֹלָמִים], everlasting righteousness, that is, righteousness sufficient for all ages, whose effects would endure through all eternity. Surely no one else can be this but our King, the Messiah [מָשִׁיחַ], the anointed one, Christ (Dan. 9:24). Even the open enemies of Christ, the Jews, agree, when they call the Messiah our righteousness [מָשִׁיחַ צִדְקֵנוּ]. For Christ became for us righteousness [ἐγενήθη ἡμῖν δικαιοσύνη], and indeed has been found to be our righteousness (1 Cor. 1:30). He, having taken the form of a servant, satisfied the law of love by his most perfect obedience, and kept both commandments, concerning the love of God and of neighbour, most exactly to his last breath. The love he owed to God bound Christ, once he was made under the law, to seek God's glory and to make it as bright as possible. This is clearly attested by the whole history of the Gospel. For already in boyhood he diligently attended to the things of his Father [ἐν τοῖς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ] (Luke 2:40, 49). Preaching the kingdom of God (Matt. 4), he vindicated his most holy law from the false glosses of the Pharisees (Matt. 5). He carried out the will of him who sent him with the greatest delight (John 4:34), and was made obedient even to death, and the death of the cross (Phil. 2:8). He revealed the name, that is, the perfections of God, and set forth especially his truth, goodness, wisdom, righteousness, holiness, and all-sufficiency, as if on a noble stage exposed to the view of all. So much so that the glory of God shone forth from this work more than from any other, even more than from the work of creation itself. Just as Christ did not seek his own glory but the glory of him who sent him [τὴν δόξαν τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτόν] (John 7:18), so too he did not seek what was his own but what belonged to his neighbour (1 Cor. 13:5). He was not ashamed to be called his brother (Heb. 2:11). For he pursued him with such affection that he did not hesitate to lay down his life for him. Christ himself testifies that no one has greater love than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends [ὑπὲρ τῶν φίλων αὐτοῦ] (John 15:13). But the Lord Jesus, superior to all human feeling, was made a curse [κατάρα] for us (Gal. 3:13), that is, a sacrifice and offering for a curse. He was, as it were, the living model and image of this, insofar as a holy man and Lord of glory could become such, bearing in body and soul the full force of the curse. Indeed, he died for us while we were still considered in ourselves ungodly and sinners [ἀσεβεῖς, ἁμαρτωλοί] and his enemies [ἐχθροί] (Rom. 5:6, 9, 10). O great love! O immeasurable charity! surpassing knowledge [ὑπερβάλλουσαν τῆς γνώσεως], whose breadth and length and depth and height no one can grasp (Eph. 3:18, 19). Thus the law of God was in the midst of his heart, that is, he fulfilled all the righteous requirements [δικαιώματα] of the law (Ps. 40:9). This was clearly prefigured long ago by the two tables of the law enclosed in the ark (Exod. 34:16, 17; Heb. 9:4).
XII.

units.la: Hanc verò, quam hactenus vidimus in Christo justitiam satis solidum omnis gloriationis nostrae fundamentum esse probatu amplius difficile non est; sicut enim maledictus, qui ponit fiduciam in homine, Jer. 17:5. ita econtra non potest non esse benedictus, qui omnem suam gloriationis fiduciam in hac sola Christi ponit justitia; illa enim non est φίλα ἀνθρώπου [?], sed θεανθρώπου [?], i.e. ejus, qui est Deus & homo in eadem persona; idem enim, qui est צמח צדיק germen justum Davidis, est simul יהוה צדקנו Jehovah justitia nostra, Jerem. 23:6. Hinc haec justitia Christi, quod emphasi non caret, vocatur δικαιωσύνη τῷ Θεῷ[?], 2. Pet. 1:1. Rom. 3:21,22. tum & quidem quàm maximè quia à tali, qui est Jehova, verus Deus, nobis fuit acquisita, Esa. 45:23,24. & 54:17. tum quia à Deo in liberrimo suo consilio nobis fuit procurata, tum quia à Deo nobis gratis datur, unde vocatur χάρισμα & δώ-ρημα, Rom.5:16,17[?]. tum quia Deum summè decet, qui per hanc justitiam sanctificatur, h.e. sanctus demonstratur, Esa.5:16[?]. & justificatur justificando impium, Rom. 3:26. unde haud immeritò gloria Dei dicitur, summa enim gloria Deo est, esse justitiam populi sui & lucem gentium; inde est, quod Hieropsaltes dicat, coelis justitiam per Christum indicantibus omnes populos vidisse כבודו gloriam ejus Psal. 97:6. mirum igitur non est, quòd fideles in justitia Christi, quae est gloria Dei glorientur.
units.tr: That this righteousness of Christ, which we have seen so far, is a sufficiently solid foundation of all our glorying, is not hard to prove further. For as cursed is the man who puts his trust in man, Jer. 17:5, so, conversely, the one who places all his confidence of glorying in this righteousness of Christ alone cannot but be blessed. For this righteousness is not of human [φίλα ἀνθρώπου] but of the God-man [θεανθρώπου], that is, of him who is God and man in one person. He who is the righteous Branch [צמח צדיק] of David is also Jehovah our righteousness [יהוה צדקנו], Jer. 23:6. Hence this righteousness of Christ, which is not without emphasis, is called the righteousness of God [δικαιωσύνη τῷ Θεῷ], 2 Pet. 1:1; Rom. 3:21, 22. It is so called especially because it was obtained for us by one who is Jehovah, the true God, Isa. 45:23, 24; 54:17; because it was procured for us by God in his most free counsel; because it is given to us freely by God, and so is called a gift of grace [χάρισμα] and a free gift [δώρημα], Rom. 5:16, 17; and because it greatly becomes God, who is sanctified through this righteousness, that is, shown to be holy, Isa. 5:16, and who is justified in justifying the ungodly, Rom. 3:26. Hence it is not undeservedly called the glory of God. For it is the greatest glory to God to be the righteousness of his people and the light of the nations. Hence the psalmist says that the heavens, declaring the righteousness of Christ, have shown all peoples his glory [כבודו], Ps. 97:6. It is no wonder, then, that believers glory in the righteousness of Christ, which is the glory of God.
XIII.

units.la: Quaeris, quomodo nos gloriari possimus in justitia alterius? Hinc quidem Christus amplam gloriationis segetem ex propriis colligit laboribus, sed qui ego in aliena justitia gloriari possim jure, non video. Resp. Ideo in eadem jure gloriari possumus, quia Christi justitia fit nostra & quidem 1. sponsione pro nobis a parte Christi, II. verâ vivaque fide a parte nostri. Sponsione, quicquid enim Christus praestitit, id omne fecit tanquam ערב ἐγγυητής[?], sponsor, vas noster, qui apud Patrem in aeterno pacto spopondit, se omnia pro electis à Parre[?] sibi datis praesticurum[?].ad quae lege Dei tenentur ne descendant in foveam, Job.33:23,24. quemadmodum hanc sponsionem vivis coloribus depictam reperimus, Psal.40:7,8,9. sasacrificio & munere non oblectabaris,&c. & sic Christus juxta hoc pactum & πληρώματι τῷ χρόνῳ [?] formam servi accepit, quatenus scilicet sub legem factus justitiam in lege promissam sub conditione perfectae obedientiae ei praestandae debuit acquirere, quod nisi fecisset, absit invidia verbo, peccasset, & peccando maledictionem legis incurrisset, quae conditio erat servilis, justitia enim & vita ipsi erat promerenda, ut mercenario salarium, quod ei non addicitur nisi post exantlatos labores, Phil.2:7,8. Hinc passim apud Prophetas vocatur servus Dei, Esa.42:1. 49:2. 53:10. 54:17. & Jehovah Dominus ejus, Psal.16. Esa. 49:4,5. Imo Christus provinciam sibi impositam sedulo accurans vocatur justus servus Dei, Esa.53:10. quatenus scilicet justificatus fuit a Deo suo, Esa.50:8. & quidem in spiritu, 1.Tim.3:16, h.e. absolutus non tantum a criminationibus hostium falso sibi impactis, sed etiam a peccatis nostris, quae sua fecerat sponsione, ita ut nec Diabolus, nec lex, nec peccatum, nec mundus quicquam haberent, quo eum accusare possent, infensissimique ejus hostes cogerentur fateri, eum esse verum Dei filium; Hinc ipse pater in dialogistica illa prophetia, Psal.16. consignata Christum ita alloquitur, dixisti ad Jehovam, Dominus es tu, h.e. verbis & factis me agnovisti Dominum, tequè Jehovae spontaneum servum stitisti, nil nisi ex praescripto meo faciens, nihil tuo arbitrio reservans, ideo טובתי [?] בל עליך bonum meum non est super te pro sanctis, qui sunt in terra, h.e. non amplius teneris gratiam meam bonaque inde dependentia acquirere, id enim praestitum est a te, ideo a sponsione te absolvo, ac sanctis, quos elegi ex mundo, tibique sanctificandos dedi, gratiam meam adjudico; sicquè per unius obedientiam multi constituuntur justi, Rom.5:19.
units.tr: You ask how we can glory in the righteousness of another. Christ indeed gathers a rich harvest of glorying from his own labours, but I do not see by what right I could glory in another's righteousness. Answer: we can rightly glory in it because the righteousness of Christ becomes ours, and this happens in two ways: 1. by his surety-undertaking on our behalf on Christ's side; II. by true and living faith on our side. By surety-undertaking. For whatever Christ has accomplished, he did as surety [ערב, ἐγγυητής], our guarantor, who in the eternal covenant promised the Father that he would perform everything for those given to him by the Father, on which terms they are bound by God's law not to go down into the pit, Job 33:23, 24. We find this undertaking vividly depicted in Ps. 40:7, 8, 9: sacrifice and offering you did not delight in, etc. And so Christ, according to this covenant, and in the fullness of time [πληρώματι τῷ χρόνῳ] took the form of a servant, in so far as, made subject to the law, he was to acquire the righteousness promised in the law, under the condition that he render it perfect obedience. If he had not done this, let me say without offence, he would have sinned, and by sinning would have incurred the curse of the law. This was a servile condition, for righteousness and life were to be earned by him, as a wage is earned by a hired labourer, which is not paid until after the labour is done, Phil. 2:7, 8. Hence he is often called servant of God by the prophets, Isa. 42:1; 49:2; 53:10; 54:17, and Jehovah is called his Lord, Ps. 16; Isa. 49:4, 5. Indeed, Christ, diligently carrying out the task laid upon him, is called the righteous servant of God, Isa. 53:10, in so far as he was justified by his God, Isa. 50:8, and indeed in the Spirit, 1 Tim. 3:16, that is, acquitted not only of the accusations falsely brought against him by his enemies, but also of our sins, which he had taken upon himself by his undertaking. So neither the devil, nor the law, nor sin, nor the world had anything with which to accuse him, and his most bitter enemies were compelled to confess that he is the true Son of God. Hence the Father himself, in that dialogue-prophecy, Ps. 16, addresses Christ thus: you have said to Jehovah, "You are my Lord", that is, you have acknowledged me as Lord by word and deed, and have placed yourself as a willing servant of Jehovah, doing nothing except by my prescription and reserving nothing for your own will. Therefore my good is not beyond you for the saints who are on earth [טובתי בל עליך], that is, you are no longer bound to acquire my grace and the blessings depending on it, for this has been accomplished by you. So I release you from the undertaking, and I award my grace to the saints whom I have chosen out of the world and given to you to be sanctified. So by the obedience of one, many are made righteous, Rom. 5:19.
XIV.

units.la: Fide : Hoc enim omne nihil nobis prodesset nisi Christum tanquam sponsorem nostrum agnoscseremus verâque fide ejus justitiam amplecteremur, nemo enim spondet pro debitore nolente. Propterea quoque spiritus Sanctus, qui est Spiritus Christi, Rom.8:9, in animis peccatorum electorum per verbum Evangelii excitat fidem, quâ ex imo miseriae suae sensu, summa sui abnegatione. Christum tanquam unicam justitiae & vitae causam, ardenti cum desiderio, fame & siti anhelant, quaerunt, desiderant, eum ut talem recipiunt, illi innituntur, in illum se reclinant, illi ut Domino suo se tradunt & mancipant, in eo solo deliciantur & gloriantur, sicque Deo gloriam dant, Rom.4:20. quo pacto arctissimè & modo quodam incomprehensibili cum Christo uniuntur; sicut talem unionem Spiritus Sanctus variis nobis depingit emblematibus, desumtis vel à rebus artificialibus, qualis est unio inter fundamentum & lapides ei superstructos, 1.Pet.1:4,5. vel à rebus physicis, qualis est inter vitem & palmites, Joh.5:1,2. inter caput & membra. 1.Cor.6:15. vel à rebus physico-moralibus, qualis est inter maritum & uxorem, Eph.5:30. His omnibus nos docens fideles vi hujus unionis unum esse in & cum Christo, Eph.5:30. Gal.2:20. & per consequens consortes omnium bonorum ejus, ita ut vita Christi fit vita nostra, in Christo enim omnes, qui pertinent ad familiam Christi, vivificabuntur, 1.Cor.15:4. justitia Christi fit justitia nostra, in ipso enim sumus justitia Dei, 2 Cor.5:21. & gloria Christi fit gloria nostra,nam in ipso sedemus in cœlis, Eph.2:6[?]. hæc enim bona sunt bona nostri capitis & mariti; quemadmodum autem maritus & uxor per matrimonium carnale non tantùm fiunt una caro, verùm etiam vi arctissimæ illius connexionis uxor bonorum mariti sui particeps redditur; sic quoquè Christus & sponsa per mysticum matrimonium non solùm fiunt unus spiritus, sed etiam sponsa omnium Christi bonorum adeoque & ejus justitiæ communione gaudet; sicuti Christus Ecclesiæ se desponsaturus inter alia etiam pro dote collaturum promittit justitiam, Hos.2,19. Hæc omnia autem fiunt sufsragante lege, quæ uti sepositâ Christi justitiâ est lex peccati & mortis, ita eâdem suppositâ est lex spiritûs & vitæ nos spiritui, justitiæ & vitæ adjudicans, Rom.8:2.
units.tr: By faith: all this would profit us nothing unless we acknowledged Christ as our surety and embraced his righteousness with true faith, for no one stands surety for an unwilling debtor. For this reason also the Holy Spirit, who is the Spirit of Christ, Rom. 8:9, stirs up faith in the hearts of the elect sinners through the word of the Gospel. By faith, from a deep sense of their misery and with the utmost self-denial, they hunger and thirst after Christ as the only cause of righteousness and life, with burning desire they seek him, long for him, receive him as such, lean on him, recline on him, surrender and give themselves to him as their Lord, and delight and glory in him alone. So they give glory to God, Rom. 4:20, and in this way they are united with Christ most closely and in a certain incomprehensible manner. The Holy Spirit depicts this union for us in various images, taken either from artificial things, such as the union between the foundation and the stones built upon it, 1 Pet. 1:4, 5; or from natural things, such as that between the vine and the branches, John 15:1, 2, between the head and the members, 1 Cor. 6:15; or from physical-moral things, such as that between the husband and the wife, Eph. 5:30. Teaching us through all these that believers, by the power of this union, are one in and with Christ, Eph. 5:30; Gal. 2:20, and consequently are partakers of all his good things. Thus the life of Christ becomes our life, for in Christ all who belong to the family of Christ shall be made alive, 1 Cor. 15:22. The righteousness of Christ becomes our righteousness, for in him we are the righteousness of God, 2 Cor. 5:21. And the glory of Christ becomes our glory, for in him we sit in the heavens, Eph. 2:6. For these goods are the goods of our head and husband. But just as husband and wife, through carnal marriage, not only become one flesh but also, by the power of that very close bond, the wife is made a sharer in her husband's goods, so also Christ and the bride, through the mystical marriage, not only become one spirit, but the bride also enjoys the fellowship of all Christ's goods, and therefore of his righteousness. Christ, about to betroth the Church to himself, promises among other things to bestow righteousness as her dowry, Hos. 2:19. All this comes about with the support of law. Just as, with Christ's righteousness set aside, the law is the law of sin and death, so with it supposed, the law is the law of the Spirit and of life, adjudging us to the Spirit, righteousness and life, Rom. 8:2.
XV.

units.la: Quia verò homini hanc justitiam anhelanti non satisfacit nuda illa scientia, pretiosum bonorum thesaurum in Christo reconditum esse, nisi ipsi certò constet & se illius participem futurum, seriò in id incumbit, ut de sua fide certus esse possit, per quam oblata illa in Christo cœlestia bona apprehendere & sua facere sciat. Ideò diligenti & accurato scrutinio certa ac infallibilia veræ vivæquè fidei gnorismata investigat, ne larvam ac speciem fidei pro ipsa fide accipiens temerè justitiam Christi sibi arroget, probè persuasus neminem esse, qui fidem non jactet, licèt interea ἃ πάντων ἡ πίστις[?], 2 Thess.3:2. fides enim vera cor nostrum à præjudiciis, falsis opiniobus de Deo ejusque viis, crassis ignorantiæ tenebris, odio Dei cupiditatibusq; carnalibus ac mundanis purificat, Act.15:9. Mundum Satanamque vincit, 1. Joh.5:4. ac omnia quæ sunt in mundo: ut τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν τῆς σαρκὸς, τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν καὶ τὴν ἀλαζονείαν τοῦ βίου, 1. Joh. 2:16. καὶ ἐνεργημένη διὰ ἀγάπην, Gal. 5:9. ita ut Deum, qui solus bonus est, cujusque bonitatis cognitio non nisi gustu addiscitur, ut Deum suum in Mediatore Jesu toto pectore intimisque amoris affectibus complectatur, utpote cujus opulentia ditatur, cujus ubertate pascitur, cujus potentia custoditur, cujus sapientia dirigitur, cujus bonitate refocillatur, denique cujus sufficientia repletur; Christum ut Salvatorem & Maritum suum defixis oculis intueatur, avidè concupiscat, arctè teneat, sinu foveat, amoris cingat brachiis, nec prius dimittat, quin in intima animæ adyta receperit, ipsiqué placere ac præcepta ejus auro desiderabiliora melleque dulciora observare summas ducat delicias; Et proximum ut creaturam ad imaginem Dei conditam fratremque suum in Christo Jesu non modò verbo & lingua ἀλλ' ἔργῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ diligat. Denique fidei quoque tribuitur ὑπακοὴν, 1.Pet.1:2. Rom.16:26. quâ anima fidelis cogitationes suas, quæ sunt inimicitia adversus Deum, sub obedientiam Christi captivat, 2.Cor.10:5. propriæ suæ voluntati, quæ nunquam non mala est, abrenunciat, se totum cum omnibus suis bonis arbitrio Jesu, ut cum iis pro lubitu agat, dedit, verbo ejus subjicit, & ita Christum ut Dominum suum non duntaxat verbis, sed etiam factis agnoscit; Et hi sunt fructus verae fidei, quos perinde profert, ac bona arbor suos fructus, ex quibus, ut etiam ex actibus fidei essentialibus, cuivis proprium cor suum in conspectu Dei ad Lydium hunc lapidem examinanti cognoscere licet, num sit in fide & per consequens particeps factus justitiæ Christi.
units.tr: But since the nuda knowledge that a precious treasure of good things is laid up in Christ does not satisfy a man who longs for this righteousness, unless he is certain that he will be a partaker of it, he applies himself earnestly to be able to be sure of his own faith, by which he knows he can apprehend and make his own those heavenly goods offered in Christ. Therefore by careful and exact scrutiny he searches out the certain and infallible marks of true and living faith, lest, taking the mask and appearance of faith for faith itself, he rashly arrogates to himself the righteousness of Christ. He is well persuaded that no one is without a claim to faith, although not all have faith [οὐ πάντων ἡ πίστις], 2 Thess. 3:2. For true faith purifies our heart from prejudices, false opinions about God and his ways, the thick darkness of ignorance, hatred of God, and fleshly and worldly desires, Acts 15:9. It overcomes the world and Satan, 1 John 5:4, and all that is in the world: the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life [τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν τῆς σαρκὸς, τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν καὶ τὴν ἀλαζονείαν τοῦ βίου], 1 John 2:16; and it is working through love [καὶ ἐνεργημένη διὰ ἀγάπην], Gal. 5:6. Thus the believer embraces God, who alone is good, and whose goodness is learned only by tasting, so that he holds his God in Jesus the Mediator with his whole heart and the inmost affections of love. He is enriched by God's abundance, fed by his fullness, kept by his power, directed by his wisdom, refreshed by his goodness, and at last filled by his sufficiency. He looks on Christ as his Saviour and Husband with fixed eyes, desires him eagerly, holds him fast, cherishes him in his bosom, embraces him with the arms of love, and does not let him go until he has received him into the innermost sanctuary of the soul. He counts it his highest delight to please him and to keep his precepts, more desirable than gold and sweeter than honey. He loves his neighbour as a creature made in the image of God and his brother in Christ Jesus, not only in word and tongue, but in deed and truth [ἀλλ' ἔργῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ]. Finally, obedience [ὑπακοὴν] is also ascribed to faith, 1 Pet. 1:2; Rom. 16:26. By it the faithful soul takes captive its thoughts, which are hostile to God, into the obedience of Christ, 2 Cor. 10:5. It renounces its own will, which is never not evil, gives itself with all its goods wholly to the disposal of Jesus, to deal with them as he pleases, submits to his word, and so acknowledges Christ as its Lord not only in words but also in deeds. These are the fruits of true faith, which it bears just as a good tree bears its fruit. From these, as also from the essential acts of faith, anyone may recognise whether he is in the faith, and consequently has been made a partaker of the righteousness of Christ, by examining his own heart in the sight of God as on the Lydian touchstone.
XVI.

units.la: Hinc ex hac fide, quâ ad Christum confugimus ut Salvatorem & eundem reveremur ut Dominum, ei ex toto corde obediendo, justitia Dei in nobis etiam revelatur ad fidem, quâ gratiâ remissionis peccatorum gloriari possumus. Et hoc est, quod Paulus ait Rom.1:17. Quicunque enim fidelis illam in Christum fidem ita in se sentit, in eodem ut Salvatore suo non potest non exultare & piè gloriari in Domino; dicens cum Ecclesia: Hilarando hilarabor in Domino, gaudebit anima mea in Deo meo, quia me induit vestibus salutis, pallio justitiæ amicivit me, ut sponsum qui applicat ornatum, & ut sponsam, quæ se operit mundo suo, Esa. 61:10. & cum Davide, Jehovah est lux mea & salus mea, à quo timebo? Jehovah robur vitæ meæ, à quo formidabo? q. d. ego quidem in me ipso sum ipsissimæ tenebræ, absque ulla vita & justitia, filius mortis, infirmitas ipsa, omniaque in hoc statu mihi occurrunt terribilia ac adversa, at per veram fidem me recipio ad Jehovam, eumque ut perfectum Salvatorem meum amplector, is lux mea, is salus mea, & robur meum, quem pavebo in cœlis? quem timebo in terris atque infernis? Et quemadmodum David gloriatur in Jehovah, sic Paulus cum toto fidelium Novi Testamenti choro gloriantur in Christo, Phil. 3:3. nos sumus circumcisio, corde circumcisi, regeniti, justificati, sanctificati, qui spiritu servimus Deo, qui non tantum externo aliquo cultu carnali labiisque nostris, sed λατρεία λογικὴ spirituali, interno veneramur Deum & gloriamur in Christo, h. e. firmiter credi-mus vitam & justitiam per Christum nobis partam esse; Sic qui nihil dignum judicavit scire, εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυρωμένον[?], 1 Cor.2:2. quippe qui est nucleus, spiritus & anima totius Veteris & Novi Testamenti, is quoque non gloriari cupit εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ χριστῷ[?], Gal. 6:14. Mirum sane, magnum illum gentium Doctorem, gloriari in ea re, quæ Judæis σκάνδαλον, Græcis μωρίαν[?] & a Deo ipso maledicta erat; sed mirari desines,si attendas, quid per hanc crucem nobis impetraverit: glorientur igitur alii in carne sua aut aliena, ac lætentur in propriis meritis; At ego supplex Deum meū ex corde oro, ne me unquam in quoquam alio gloriari sinat, quàm in justitia Christi per obedientiam ad mortem usquè, mortem autem crucis mihi adducta.
units.tr: Hence, from this faith, by which we flee to Christ as Saviour and at the same time reverence him as Lord, obeying him with our whole heart, the righteousness of God is also revealed in us unto faith, by which through the grace of the forgiveness of sins we can glory. This is what Paul means at Rom. 1:17. For whoever feels such faith in Christ within himself cannot but exult in his Saviour and glory piously in the Lord, saying with the Church: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God, for he has clothed me with garments of salvation and covered me with a robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom who puts on his finery and as a bride who adorns herself with her jewels, Isa. 61:10. And with David: The Lord is my light and my salvation; of whom shall I be afraid? The Lord is the strength of my life; whom shall I dread? That is to say: I in myself am sheer darkness, without any life or righteousness, a son of death, weakness itself, and everything in this state appears to me as terrible and adverse. But through true faith I betake myself to Jehovah and embrace him as my perfect Saviour. He is my light, my salvation and my strength. Whom shall I dread in heaven? Whom shall I fear on earth or in hell? And just as David glories in Jehovah, so Paul, with the whole choir of the faithful of the New Testament, glories in Christ (Phil. 3:3): We are the circumcision, who are circumcised in heart, born again, justified, sanctified, who serve God in the Spirit; who worship God not only with some outward carnal ritual and with our lips, but with a spiritual, inward λατρεία λογικὴ [reasonable service], and glory in Christ, that is, we firmly believe that life and righteousness have been won for us through Christ. So he who judged that he knew nothing [εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυρωμένον], 1 Cor. 2:2. Since he is the kernel, spirit and soul of the whole Old and New Testament, he too wishes to glory in nothing except [εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ] the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, Gal. 6:14. It is indeed remarkable that that great teacher of the Gentiles gloried in that which was a stumbling block [σκάνδαλον] to the Jews, foolishness [μωρίαν] to the Greeks, and cursed by God himself. But you will cease to wonder if you consider what he obtained for us through this cross. Let others, then, glory in their own flesh or in that of others, and rejoice in their own merits. But I, as a suppliant, pray to my God from my whole heart that he never allow me to glory in anything else than in the righteousness of Christ, through obedience even unto death, and the death of the cross brought upon me.
XVIII.

units.la: Sed sane neque hîc subsistit animæ fidelis gloriatio. Hactenus & hypocritæ exultare & luce verbi Evangelii lætari videntur; sed ingruente afflictionum æstu deficiunt ut herba, cui non est radix, Matth. 30:20, 21. Longè altiores radices egit hæc gloriatio fidelium, quàm ut tam citò torrefacta evanescat; inde est quòd & altius excrescat & fructum ferat in patientia, Luc. 8:15. & quando illi animum despondent, hi vires sumunt, se erigunt, & revera vel in ipsis afflictionibꝰ triumphant.
units.tr: But the believing soul's boasting does not stop even here. Hitherto hypocrites too seem to exult and rejoice in the light of the Gospel word; but when the heat of afflictions rises, they wither away like grass that has no root (Matth. 30:20, 21). The boasting of the faithful has struck far deeper roots than to wither so quickly when scorched. Hence it grows higher and bears fruit in patience (Luke 8:15). And when those others lose heart, these take strength, raise themselves up, and indeed triumph even in the afflictions themselves.

units.la: Tanta enim sæpe fidelibus contingit πληροφορία[?], quæ conscientiam plane tranquillat, intimis gaudiis lætificat, consolationibus suavissimis replet, maximas animi ægritudines dispellit, omnibusque amarissimis etiam amaritudinibus dulcorandis solum sufficit, ut non tantum glorientur ἐπ' ἐλπίδι τῆς δόξης[?] Deum nempe se in illis ut divitem, potentem, misericordem, justum, veracem, verbo ut dicam, Deum eorum, in hac & futura vita glorificaturum, sed etiam ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν[?], quæ spe imminuere, fideq; debilitare videntur: plenissimè persuasi Deum esse Deum ac patrem suum benignum in Christo Jesu, ut possint gloriari cum Davide: Jehovah est meus, non timebo, quid faciet mihi homo? Psal.115:6. sciunt quoque se ita à Deo custodiri, tam arctè cum Christo inexpugnabili illa rupe unitos esse, ut ei innixi adversus omnes procellas atque adeò contra inferni portas inconcussi maneant, nec ab ullo hoste vinci aut ab amore benedicti Servatoris separari possint. Psal.125:2. Rom.8:35,37. porrò hunc Deum benignum mala ista & afflictiones ita moderari, ut fideles ea perferre possint,
units.tr: For the faithful often experience such a full assurance [πληροφορία] that it completely calms the conscience, gladdens with the inmost joys, fills them with the sweetest consolations, drives away the greatest distresses of mind, and alone is sufficient to sweeten all the bitterest bitterness. So they glory not only in the hope of glory [ἐπ' ἐλπίδι τῆς δόξης], namely that God, rich, powerful, merciful, just and true, in a word their God, will glorify himself in them in this life and the life to come, but also in tribulations [ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν], which seem to diminish hope and weaken faith. Fully persuaded that God is their gracious God and Father in Christ Jesus, they can glory with David: Jehovah is mine, I will not fear; what can man do to me? (Psal. 115:6). They also know that they are so kept by God, and so closely united with Christ, that, leaning on that unconquerable rock, they remain unshaken against all storms and even against the gates of hell, and cannot be conquered by any enemy nor separated from the love of the blessed Saviour (Psal. 125:2; Rom. 8:35, 37). Moreover, this gracious God so moderates these evils and afflictions that the faithful are able to bear them,

units.la: 1. Cor. 10:13. omniaque cooperari in ipsorum bonum. Rom. 8:28. Esa.49:16. ac nominatim tribulationes & ærumnas gratiâ Dei & merito Christi non esse signa iræ, sed amoris. Heb.12:6,8. utpote quæ sunt παιδεία[?] ad fideles emendandos, sanctificandos, humiliandos, & excitandos ad timorem & venerationem Dei ut Dei sancti, qui etiam peccata suorum non potest dissimulare, Psal. 119: 75. Jerem.46:27. 2.Cor.4:16. & γυμνασίαν, δοκιμασίαν, πειρασμοί[?], quibus patientia, fides, charitas, spes aliæque virtutes, ut aurum in igne probantur & manifestantur, Rom. 5:3,4. Heb.12:11. 1.Pet.1:6,7. quin etiam se Christo capiti suo per has passiones conformes fieri, crucisque ejus communione gaudere, Rom.8:17. Phil.3,10. 2.Cor.4: 8,9. ac tandem ab omnibus malis & afflictionibus liberatum iri & per ipsam mortem transituros ad vitam æternam Psal.34:20. Act.14:22. Atquè ita victrix evadit anima fidelis in laboribus omnibus, jacturis & ærumnis, bene persuasa, quicquid in creatura passa est detrimenti, repensum iri cum auctario à creatore, jacturam æris pari pondere auri, afflictionis levitatem longè gravissimô pondere gloriæ,1.Cor.6:17. cujꝰ quidé gloriæ,parte(totiꝰ itaq; pignꝰ)nunc recipit anima in antecessu,in eaq; inter omnis generis ærumnas ac perpessiones gaudiô ineffabili & gloriosô exultat; cujus cœlestis gaudii mediis in tribulationibus clarissima vestigia efficacissimè expressa videmus in divis Apostolis, qui gaudebant, quòd digni haberentur,qui pro ejus nomine contumeliâ afficerentur, Act. 5:41♦ in Sancto Paulo, qui superabundabat latitiâ in omni afflictione sua, 2.Cor.7:4♦ fidisquè Christo Martyribus,qui ad immanissima tormenta tanquam ad lautissimas epulas læti cantantesquè iverunt,acerbissimisquè in doloribus jubilarunt. O igitur felices terquè beati fideles, quorum fides tam viva ac robusta, ut nullis afflictionum aquis extingui nec à morte ipsa vinci possit! Faxit nunc Deus, ut quæ de hac gloriatione, quæ medulla totius Christianismi est, protulimus, magis ac magis in nostra conscientia experiamur nihil nobis, sed omnia gloriæ gratiæ Christi tribuentes, ut si quando gloriamur,in Domino gloriemur,ita sit Domine Jesu. Amen.
units.tr: (1 Cor. 10:13) and that all things work together for their good (Rom. 8:28; Isa. 49:16). And in particular, that tribulations and distresses, through the grace of God and the merit of Christ, are signs not of wrath but of love (Heb. 12:6, 8). For they are chastening [παιδεία] to amend, sanctify and humble the faithful, and to rouse them to the fear and reverence of God as the holy God, who cannot overlook even the sins of his own (Psal. 119:75; Jer. 46:27; 2 Cor. 4:16). They are also training [γυμνασίαν], testing [δοκιμασίαν] and trials [πειρασμοί], by which patience, faith, love, hope and the other virtues are proved and made manifest, as gold is in the fire (Rom. 5:3, 4; Heb. 12:11; 1 Pet. 1:6, 7). Indeed, through these sufferings they are made conformable to Christ their head and rejoice in the fellowship of his cross (Rom. 8:17; Phil. 3:10; 2 Cor. 4:8, 9). And at last they will be freed from all evils and afflictions and, through death itself, pass over to eternal life (Psal. 34:20; Acts 14:22). And so the believing soul emerges victorious in all labours, losses and distresses, well persuaded that whatever it has lost in the creature will be repaid by the Creator with interest: the loss of copper with an equal weight of gold, the lightness of affliction with a far heavier weight of glory (1 Cor. 6:17). Of this glory the soul now receives a part in advance, as the pledge of the whole, and in it, amid all kinds of distress and suffering, it exults with unspeakable and glorious joy. We see the clearest traces of this heavenly joy, most effectively expressed amid tribulations, in the divine apostles, who rejoiced that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonour for his name (Acts 5:41); in St Paul, who overflowed with joy in all his affliction (2 Cor. 7:4); and in the faithful martyrs, who went joyfully and singing to the most savage torments as to the most sumptuous feasts, and shouted for joy in the bitterest pains. O therefore happy, thrice blessed believers, whose faith is so lively and robust that no waters of affliction can quench it, and not even death can conquer it! May God now grant that we experience ever more in our conscience what we have set forth about this boasting, which is the marrow of all Christianity: ascribing nothing to ourselves but everything to the glory of the grace of Christ, so that whenever we glory, we may glory in the Lord. So be it, Lord Jesus. Amen.
